_about: What each node on the Status page is for, what uses it, and a real example. Keyed by the node's short name (a container's name without skippycore-/skippytel- and without the -1 on the end; a model's or service's own name). A new node means a new entry here; portal/tests/test_status_nodes.py fails on a stale one. `usage` fields are filled live from what the machine reports (core/reporter).

mentat.for: The physics, chemistry and maths answerer. You (or Skippy) ask a question in plain words; Mentat works out which sigma-ground calculation it is, runs it, and answers with the value, its unit, the formula and the source. It never makes a number up: no source, no number.
used_by: Skippy's chats, public and private (ask_mentat, forced when a reply claims physics)
the Experiments playground (the cloud copy, keywords only)

example.ask: If I throw a baseball at 45 degrees at 100 miles per hour, how far will it travel before it touches the ground?
example.answer: 203.8 m (range at 45° and 44.7 m/s, no air). Source: sigma_ground.materia (projectile_motion). Derived, 230 ms.

mentat.note: Almost every call is a plain question (/ask); the 200+ individual tools are rarely called by name. Showing all of them to a chat cost about 73,000 tokens of its context, so over MCP Mentat now shows only three tools (ask, find_tools, call_tool); the full set is still on REST /tools/<name> and any tool can still be called by name.

llm.for: skippy-core's model server (llama-swap). It holds the chat, coder, router and vision models and loads the one a request names.
used_by: the Ollama shim that old services still call

searxng.for: A self-hosted web search engine. It asks several public search engines for you and returns plain results, with no account, no key and no tracking.

example.answer: Title, URL and a one-line snippet for the top six results.

mosquitto.for: The message broker between the car's logger and the car reader. TeslaMate publishes the car's live state to it; it keeps the last value of every topic on disk.

tesla-db.for: TeslaMate's Postgres database: every drive and charge the car has logged.

teslamate.for: Logs the Tesla's drives, charges and state around the clock from Tesla's own API, without waking the car. Its page (tailnet only, port 4000) is where the Tesla sign-in is kept.
used_by: the Car tile and Skippy's car_status (through the reader)

car.for: The car reader: keeps the latest values the broker has (charge, lock, location) and serves them as one small answer with the readiness contract.

chat.for: The resident chat model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). It answers the public Skippy chat, writes chat names and summaries, and is the 'skippy-chat' that old services ask for.
used_by: WebFetch's page summariser in Core runs

coder.for: The coding model behind the private Skippy (Claude Code on Core's own brain).

router.for: A small fast model that reads a physics question and picks the Mentat calculation to run.

vision.for: Looks at pictures: describes screenshots and photos, copies out the words in them.
used_by: the private Skippy's eyes (pictures the Core coder cannot read)
